chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about an elderly man who is too weak to fast during the month of Ramadan. He said: 'He should give in charity the equivalent of feeding one poor person for each day.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for an elderly person who cannot fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific mechanism of fidyah for the elderly or chronically ill who cannot fast, mandating the provision of one meal per missed day. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing the compensation to be fulfilled through direct feeding rather than monetary payment, emphasizing the social welfare aspect of Ramadan obligations.
